newsitem.title: UK: Sterling off highs but holds above support in Euro.
newsitem.headline: Sterling off highs but holds above support in Euro.

text.p: Sterling lost some of its earlier momentum at midday on Monday but managed to retain its foothold above support at $1.6750.
European and domestic politics were keeping sterling markets ticking over on Monday but activity was subdued ahead of a raft of U.K. economic indicators later this week.
The U.K. PSBR for November is due at 0930 GMT on Tuesday whith November unemployment and retail sales at 0930 GMT on Wednesday.
"The retail sales and unemployment numbers are particularly important," said Julian Jessop, chief European economist at Nikko Europe.
Markets are also awaiting a key parliamentary vote later on Monday, but analysts said there would be little effect even if the government is defeated.

"The market has already taken on board a lot of political uncertainty. So I don't think it will be particularly upset if the vote goes against the government," said Leo Doyle, economist at Kleinwort Benson.
Analysts said while they expected the government could be defeated in a vote at 2200 GMT on its negotiating stance on the European Union's common fisheries policy, a motion of confidence is unlikely.
"No chance. No chance at all," said Nikko's Jessop when asked if a vote of confidence was likely.
"Anybody who follows the U.K. will know this is a non-issue," he added.
At 1253 GMT sterling/dollar was trading at $1.6596/06 against 1.6585/95 in late Europe on Friday.
Political wrangles at home are unlikely to take much of the shine off sterling, said analysts.
Doyle said higher interest rates are still expected by U.K. markets, and that should be enough to keep sterling buoyed.
"Fundamentals are such that sterling will remain strong," said Doyle.

European markets were also digesting the EU budget stability pact which approved strict budget deficit limits for monetary union participants but allowed for political decision-making on whether fines are to be levied on those countries which overspend.
The fact that a stability agreement was reached, said analysts, is bad for the mark and positive for other EMS currencies.
For sterling, the impact of the EU stability pact was indirect, said Jessop.
"The impact is indirect. The extent the dollar has benefitted from deutschemark weakness, that is dragging up sterling as well," said Nikko's Jessop.
At 1259 GMT sterling/mark stood at 2.500/10 against 2.5645/55 in late Europe.
